title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood’s recommended processes, checklists, and guardrails for onboarding models into the Applied ML eval harness, maintaining prompt/benchmark catalogs, defining quantization profiles, and executing regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied-research engineers, and platform integrators responsible for model onboarding and ongoing quality monitoring.

Goals:
- Provide a single, repeatable onboarding flow for new models and model updates.
- Define standards for prompt sets and benchmarks used by continuous quality monitoring.
- Describe quantization profile creation and validation steps to preserve quality while reducing cost.
- Define a regression triage process and escalation paths for detected quality drops.

Scope:
- Applies to all models intended for serving in Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private environments and to evaluation harness artifacts stored in the eval catalog.
- Excludes proprietary customer prompt material that is covered by customer-specific NDAs; see related customer onboarding docs for those flows.

Owners & Roles:
- Model Owner: Primary contact for a model (onboarding, test case sign-off).
- Applied ML Lead: Responsible for final acceptance into the eval catalog.
- Eval Harness SRE: Runs CI/CD jobs, alerts, and maintains harness infra.
- Regression Triage SME: Leads triage meetings and assigns bug fixes or rollback tasks.

Onboarding checklist (high level):
1) Pre-onboard triage: confirm model license, compatibility with runtime (supported ops, tokenizer), and target quantization modes.
2) Baseline evaluation: run the model against the model onboarding prompt set (see Prompt Sets section). Capture metrics: exact-match, BLEU, chrF, ROUGE-L (where applicable), and embedding-based similarity on semantic tasks.
3) Latency & cost profiling: run the benchmarking suite at representative prompt length distributions to capture p50/p95 latency, throughput, and per-token GPU/CPU cost estimates.
4) Quantization profiling (if applicable): create an initial 8-bit/4-bit profile per the Quantization Profiles section. Validate degradation thresholds.
5) Quality guardrails: run the model through the toxicity/safety filters, hallucination detectors, and structured-output validators.
6) Sign-off: model owner and Applied ML Lead sign acceptance document and add model to the eval catalog with a pinned version and metadata (training data provenance, license, recommended profiles).

Prompt sets & benchmark guidance:
- Structure: Prompt sets must be grouped into categories: core-capabilities, domain-specific, failure-mode probes, and regression-cases. Each prompt must include: id, short description, seed prompt, expected output constraints (regex or schema), and a golden reference when feasible.
- Sizing: Minimum 200 prompts for core-capabilities per model family, 50-100 for domain-specific sets. Regression case catalog should be prioritized by customer impact (top 50).
- Labeling & versioning: Every prompt set is versioned in the eval catalog. Use semantic versioning: major for schema changes, minor for new prompts, patch for corrections.
- Example prompt metadata (text format):
  id: prompt_core_sm_summary_v1_001
  description: Summarization of short news paragraph
  prompt: "Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence:
  ..."
  expected: short factual summary (max 32 tokens)

Quality metrics to gather per prompt-set run:
- Accuracy metrics: exact-match, F1, task-specific scores.
- Calibration: confidence distribution, top-1 vs. top-2 probabilities (when available).
- Safety: toxicity scores (Perspective API or internal classifier), PII redaction failures.
- Semantic similarity: embedding cosine to golden reference.

Quantization profiles & validation steps:
- Goal: Reduce model size and per-token cost while bounding quality regressions within agreed thresholds (default thresholds described below).
- Standard profiles:
  - fp16 (baseline)
  - int8 (dynamic/static) recommended for production when p95 latency meets SLOs
  - int4 (experimental) for low-cost inference; requires stricter validation
- Profile metadata required: quantization-mode, per-layer exceptions, calibration dataset id, representative sequence lengths, observed memory reduction, and per-batch latency overhead.
- Validation steps:
  1. Run the quantized model against the full onboarding core-capabilities prompt set.
  2. Compare key metrics to baseline (fp16): per-prompt delta and aggregated AUC.
  3. Apply the gating rule: fail the profile if any of the following occur:
     - Absolute drop in task-specific metric > 3.0% (default)
     - Increase in safety failures (toxicity/PII) > 1.0% absolute
     - Semantic-similarity cosine drop > 0.02 average
  4. If profile fails, iterate with per-layer exclusions or higher-precision for embedding/LM head.

Regression detection & triage playbook:
- Detection sources: nightly eval runs, production quality monitoring (sampled prompts), customer-reported cases, model rollout A/B comparisons.
- Initial triage (within 4 hours of alert):
  1. Triage owner (on-call Applied ML) acknowledges and captures: model-version, pipeline-id, job-run-id, observed delta and affected prompt sets.
  2. Re-run failing prompt set in isolated CI with exact harness config to reproduce.
  3. Compare against baseline run artifacts (stored in eval catalog): metric diffs, raw outputs, and seed RNG state if used.
- Classification rubric:
  - Type A: Model-regression (quality drop due to model weights or tokenizer changes).
  - Type B: Serving/regression (inference runtime or quantization degradation).
  - Type C: Data/regression (prompt set changes, input normalization issues).
- Response actions by classification:
  - Type A: Notify model owner, revert to prior pinned version or roll forward with hotfix model. Initiate model-retraining/weight-delta investigation.
  - Type B: Rollback quantization profile or runtime change; capture performance counters; route to Serving Runtime team.
  - Type C: Reconcile prompt/input normalization; update prompt-set version and rebaseline.
- Escalation matrix:
  - 0-4 hours: Triage & reproduce (Applied ML on-call).
  - 4-24 hours: Mitigation (rollback or traffic-shift) and root-cause hypothesis.
  - >24 hours: Cross-functional incident review, customer communication, and exec notification if high-impact.

Runbook snippets & CLI examples:
- Run the onboarding eval job (example):
  REDWOOD_ENV=staging 
  ./bin/eval-runner --model rwd-llama-70b --prompt-set core-capabilities-v1 --profile fp16 --output s3://eval-artifacts/rwd-llama-70b/onboard-2026-09-01

- Example compare command (produces a regression report):
  ./bin/eval-compare --baseline s3://eval-artifacts/rwd-llama-70b/baseline-2026-08-15 
    --candidate s3://eval-artifacts/rwd-llama-70b/onboard-2026-09-01 --metrics summary,semantic,safety --out report.json

Golden artifacts & storage conventions:
- All eval run artifacts are stored in the eval-artifacts bucket with the path convention: s3://eval-artifacts/{model}/{run-id}/. Each run contains: metrics.json, outputs.jsonl, config.yml, seed.txt, and smoke.log.
- Baseline runs must be pinned in the model metadata and referenced in the model registry entry.

SLOs & thresholds (recommendations):
- Nightly regression alert threshold: aggregate metric delta > 1.5% absolute on core-capabilities OR any single high-priority regression-case failure.
- Quantization acceptance thresholds (defaults): see Quantization Profiles section (3% metric drop, 1% safety increase).
- Latency SLOs captured separately in infra/perf standards; include p95 latency and fail-open policies in model metadata.

Communication & documentation:
- All onboarding steps, decisions, and accepted profiles must be recorded in the model registry entry and linked in the eval catalog.
- Regression triage outcomes require a postmortem document when mitigation takes >24 hours or rollback affects >5% of customer traffic.

Audit & compliance notes:
- For private deployments, ensure quantization calibration datasets do not contain customer PII unless contractually permitted.
- Keep an audit log entry for every model promotion, quantization profile activation, and rollback with actor and timestamp.

Appendix: Example config.yml (text):
  model: rwd-llama-70b
  run_id: onboard-2026-09-01
  prompt_set: core-capabilities-v1
  profile: int8-dynamic
  hardware: g4dn.12xlarge
  seq_lengths: [64, 256, 1024]
  metrics: [accuracy,semantic,safety,latency]
